CFDocument.creator: Alabama State Department of Education
CFDocument.title: Health Education (2019)
CFDocument.description:
The 2019 Alabama Course of Study: Health Education describes the minimum required content for a curriculum that focuses on the development of health-literate citizens. This course of study reflects current evidence-based health information regarding disease prevention and health. The prior course of study was primarily topic-based, while the new course of study is skill-based with topics integrated within the standards. The instructional foundation for Alabama’s K-12 health education program provides guidance on the essential skills and knowledge that students should have at each grade level. The health education program incorporates national health education standards, the six dimensions of health, and the priority health-risk behaviors and experiences that most influence adolescent health, as identified by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The sequence of content across grade levels provides for increasing degrees of complexity appropriate for students’ developmental levels from early childhood through adolescence.
Standards define what students should know and be able to do at the conclusion of a course or grade. Each content standard completes the stem “Students can...” Standards do not dictate curriculum or teaching methods. Content standards in this document contain minimum required content. The order in which standards are listed within a course or grade is not intended to convey a sequence for instruction. For example, one topic may appear before a second in the standards for a given grade, but this does not necessarily mean that the first must be taught before the second. A teacher might prefer to teach the second topic before the first topic or might choose to highlight connections by teaching both topics at the same time. In addition, a teacher might prefer to teach a topic of his or her own choosing that leads to students mastering the standards for both topics.

CFItems.fullStatement: Model refusal skills that avoid or reduce health risks.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: role playing how to effectively handle bullying, harassment, and peer pressure situations_

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate skills that avoid conflict.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: asking someone respectfully not to smoke, practice active listening, reacting sensibly, communicating clearly, practicing patience_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 5: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health. (Decision-Making)
Distinguish when a self-decision should be made or if help should be sought from a responsible adult.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: friends begin drinking, unsafe situation arises at school, suicidal friend, suspected abuse, seat belt use, suicidal thoughts_

CFItems.fullStatement: Determine when it is necessary to ask for assistance when making a health choice.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: friend begins to self-harm, negative peer pressure_

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze healthy alternatives over unhealthy alternatives when making decisions.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: eating regular meals vs. skipping meals, choosing healthy snacks vs. junk food, getting proper exercise vs. too much screen time_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 6: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health. (Goal-Setting)
Assess current personal health practices and set a goal to adopt, maintain, or improve one or more health practices.
Describe changing abilities, priorities, and responsibilities that impact personal health goals.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: age, injuries, changing jobs, leaving active school life to work, sedentary to walking, walking to jogging, jogging to running; eating poorly to making healthy food choices leading to weight loss or weight gain_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 7: Students will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks. (Self-Management)
State the importance of assuming responsibility for personal health behaviors and avoiding risky behaviors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: fast food vs. My Plate recommendations, screen time vs. active living_

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate healthy practices and behaviors that will maintain or improve the health of self and others.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: practicing proper use of prescription medications, good nutrition, proper rest, regular exercise; avoiding driver distractions_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 8: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health. (Advocacy)
Create ways to influence and support others in making positive health choices.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: using social media campaigns, YouTube live campaign, posters; addressing local school board with the need for quality physical education and healthier food choices_

CFItems.fullStatement: Describe which advertising appeals are being used in various advertisements.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: bandwagon appeal, brand loyalty appeal, sex appeal_

CFItems.fullStatement: Grade 8
Anchor Standard 1: Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health. (Health Promotion)
Explain how emotional, intellectual, physical, spiritual, mental, and social health affect each other.
Determine how social influences can affect physical health.
Describe how risky health behaviors affect the emotional, physical, and social health of adolescents.
Analyze how the environment, family history, personal behaviors, and health care can affect individual healthful living.
Describe ways to reduce or prevent injuries and illness in adolescents as it pertains to family history, personal behaviors, and health care.
Create a plan for eliminating personal unhealthy behaviors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: inappropriate use of needles, tobacco use, physical inactivity, sexual contact, alcohol consumption, inadequate sleep_

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze the relationship between engaging in regular physical activity and healthy eating as ways to improve personal health.
Analyze family history to determine the effects of health conditions that may be chronic or acute diseases.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: diabetes, high-cholesterol, high blood pressure, cancer, mental health issues_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 2: Students will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors. (Analyzing Influences)
Describe the influence of culture on health beliefs, practices, and behaviors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: religious beliefs, gang activity, family customs_

CFItems.fullStatement: Examine ways the school and community encourage students to use appropriate life skills to improve health.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: participating in conflict resolution practices, Red Ribbon Week, Walk to School Day_

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze the influences of technology on personal and family health.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: screen time, video game addictions, activity trackers, diabetes monitor, heart monitor, fitness assessment tools_

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain how societal perceptions influence healthy and unhealthy behaviors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: acceptance of teenage smoking and teenage pregnancy by peers, certain communities, and cultures_

CFItems.fullStatement: Give examples of how substance abuse can increase the likelihood of other health risk behaviors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: alcohol consumption lowering inhibitions, e-cigarettes or vaping leading to smoking_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 3: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid information, products, and services to enhance health. (Access to Information/ Products/ Services)
Analyze the validity of health claims made concerning health products and services.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: use of herbal medicines, nutritional supplements, weight loss supplements, steroids use_

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify situations that may require professional health services, including self-harm, suicidal thoughts, substance abuse, sexual abuse, and harm toward others.
Anchor Standard 4: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks. (Interpersonal Communication)
Analyze how strategies using verbal and nonverbal communication effectively can enhance health.
CFItems.notes:
_Examples: verbal -- using positive interpersonal communication to avoid conflict_

_non-verbal -- shaking hands, displaying positive facial expressions, making eye contact_

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate negotiation skills which help resolve conflict in bullying situations.
Demonstrate effective communication when confronted with mental or emotional problems in others.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: respect vs. disrespect, empathy vs. complacency, calmness vs. excitability, confronting vs. non-confrontational_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 5: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health. (Decision-Making)
Predict the impact on self and others when making a health-related decision.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: following a time-management plan, walking to school, limiting caffeine intake, riding with an impaired driver_

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze options as well as outcomes, when pressured by peers to perform illegal acts.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: underage drinking leading to being arrested, injury or death when not wearing a seat belt, riding a motorcycle without a helmet resulting in head injury_

CFItems.fullStatement: Critique the positive and negative outcomes of a health-related decision.
CFItems.notes:
_Examples: positive -- keeping calendar to manage time, reading food labels, getting adequate sleep_

_negative -- tobacco use, eating disorders, drug use_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 6: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health. (Goal-Setting)
Apply strategies and skills needed to attain a personal health goal.
Analyze how keeping an activity record will help an individual to attain a personal health goal.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: using food journal to track nutritional intake, My Fitness Pal, Fitbit, digital tracking device, track daily activity with activity log_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 7: Students will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks. (Self-Management)
Perform overall self-assessments and identify behaviors that will impact personal health.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: assessing sleeping, eating, and exercising patterns_

CFItems.fullStatement: Document healthy practices and behaviors that will improve the health of self and others.
CFItems.notes: _Example: maintaining a personal health journal_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 8: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health. (Advocacy)
Demonstrate ways to influence and support others in making positive health choices.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: public service announcements, persuasive writing, YouTube videos, skits_

CFItems.fullStatement: Work collaboratively to advocate for healthy individuals, families, and schools.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: designing healthy recipes, supporting the school wellness policy, school newscasts, school newsletters_

CFItems.fullStatement: Health Education
CFItems.notes: This is a half-credit course which is required for graduation. It is recommended that students take this course in Grade 10.

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 1: Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health. (Health Promotion)
Predict how health literacy and behaviors can affect health status.
Describe the interrelationships of emotional, mental, physical, social, spiritual, and environmental health.
Identify symptoms and methods of treatment of mental health disorders, including depression, and stress.
Identify warning signs and prevention strategies for suicide.
Analyze how genetics and family history can impact personal health.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: family history of heart disease, diabetes, cancer, or addictions_

CFItems.fullStatement: Propose ways to prevent, reduce, and treat injuries and other health problems.
Determine when professional health services may be required for injury or disease.
Perform CPR, AED techniques, and First Aid procedures, including the principles of RICE (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
Analyze the relationship between access to health care and health status.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: relationship between health insurance coverage and life expectancy; access to medical care including primary care physician, hospital, vaccines_

CFItems.fullStatement: Compare and contrast the benefits of and barriers to practicing a variety of healthy behaviors.
Identify factors that impact nutritional choices.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: planning healthy meals, accessibility of healthy and unhealthy foods_

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze the potential susceptibility to and severity of injury or illness if engaging in unhealthy behaviors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: possible consequences of driving under the influence, distracted driving, not taking required medications_

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain the progression of HIV and AIDS.
Explain the progression of Type II diabetes.
Anchor Standard 2: Students will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors. (Analyzing Influences)
Analyze the influence of external factors on health beliefs and behaviors.
Analyze how family, culture, school, and community influence the health practice and behaviors of individuals.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: explaining how holiday celebrations and traditions such as over indulgence in eating and consuming alcohol affect health behaviors; explaining how extra-curricular activities and schedules result in over-consumption of fast food_

CFItems.fullStatement: Examine how peers influence healthy and unhealthy behaviors.
Critique the effect of media on personal and family health.
CFItems.notes: _Example: influence of media on teen body image, sexual activity, drugs, alcohol, violence, cyber-bullying_

CFItems.fullStatement: Cite evidence of how public health policies and government regulations can influence health promotion and disease prevention.
Describe the pros and cons of the use of technology as it affects personal, family, and community health.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: positive and negative influences on self-esteem, addiction to technology, personal interactions and relationships_

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze how the perceptions of norms influence healthy and unhealthy behaviors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: addressing topics such as wearing safety equipment, teen pregnancy, drug abuse, suicide, cyber-bullying, weight management, potentially dangerous social media trends_

CFItems.fullStatement: Critique the influence of personal values and beliefs on individual health practices and behaviors.
Analyze how some health risk behaviors can influence the likelihood of engaging in unhealthy behaviors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: assessing the effects of driving under the influence, drinking alcohol which can lead to poor choices such as sexual behavior, poor nutrition, sedentary lifestyle_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 3: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid information, products, and services to enhance health. (Access to Information/ Products/ Services)
Evaluate the accessibility and validity of health information, products, and services.
CFItems.notes: _Example: determining the credibility of resources both online and offline_

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze valid resources from home, school, and community that provide health information.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: websites, phone apps, media ads; rape, crisis, and suicide centers_

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain laws relating to child pornography, age of consent, and sexual exploitation.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: information concerning the laws prohibiting sexual abuse; the need to report sexual abuse and legal options available to victims; laws relating to sexting and child pornography_

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain current laws related to underage drinking, distracted driving, and driving under the influence.
Identify the necessity to seek help for mental and emotional health problems.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: mood disorders, depression, anxiety and suicidal ideation_

CFItems.fullStatement: Locate information on how to cope with and rebuff unwanted physical and verbal exploitation by other persons.
Anchor Standard 4: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks. (Interpersonal Communication)
Describe skills for communicating effectively with family, peers, and others to enhance health.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: active listening, friendliness, confidence, positive feedback, empathy, respect, understanding nonverbal cues, responsiveness_

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate refusal, negotiation, and collaboration skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks.
Develop strategies to prevent, manage, or resolve interpersonal conflicts without harming self or others.
Identify warning signs of unhealthy relationships.
Differentiate between negative and positive behaviors used in conflict situations.
Demonstrate how to ask for and offer assistance to enhance the health of self and others.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: accessing crisis hotlines for suicide, sexual and physical abuse, and human trafficking; community resource materials_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 5: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health. (Decision-Making)
Examine barriers that can hinder healthy decision-making.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: peer pressure, cultural pressures, socio-economic status_

CFItems.fullStatement: Develop a thoughtful decision-making process in health-related situations.
Predict the potential short-term and long-term impact of various alternatives on self and others.
Identify warning signs of suicide in self and others and discuss effective coping skills.
Demonstrate refusal skills and explain when to use them in high risk situations.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: Saying no to sex, alcohol, and other drugs_

CFItems.fullStatement: Justify the appropriateness of individual vs. collaborative decision-making in various situations.
CFItems.notes: _Example: explaining when input from a health professional, counselor, or trusted adult would be helpful_

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze the benefits of practicing sexual abstinence.
Identify the types, symptoms, and risks of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).
Assess the consequences of teen pregnancy.
Recommend personal strategies to avoid violence or criminal activities.
Anchor Standard 6: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health. (Goal-Setting)
Assess personal health status and health practices to establish a baseline for setting health and fitness goals.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: blood pressure, resting heart rate, BMI, vaccination status_

CFItems.fullStatement: Set long-term goals for achieving optimal health and implement short-term steps to reach the goals.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: assess current health and fitness status, develop plans based on assessment results, implement and monitor plans_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 7: Students will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks. (Self-Management)
Analyze the role of individual responsibility for enhancing health.
Describe healthy practices and behaviors that will maintain or improve the health of self and others.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: effective communication skills and safety techniques, reading and understanding medicine labels, immunizations, wellness checkups and compliance_

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify negative behaviors that increase health risks to self and others.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: distracted driving, drinking and driving, illegal drug use, vaping, smoking, unprotected sex, behaviors resulting in intentional or unintentional injuries, poor eating habits, physical inactivity_

CFItems.fullStatement: Compare and contrast the responsibilities of both parents in teen parenting.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: shared responsibilities; social, financial and educational challenges_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 8: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health. (Advocacy)
Utilize accurate peer and societal norms to formulate a health enhancing message.
CFItems.notes: _Example: using data on local health issues to develop a positive message concerning a topic_

CFItems.fullStatement: Formulate and implement a list of innovative ways to influence and support others in making positive health choices.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: wearing colors for awareness, speaking to a group or individuals, making good nutritional choices_

CFItems.fullStatement: Work cooperatively as an advocate for improving personal and community health.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: student-led events, community fundraisers, national events, signing a pledge to abstain from alcohol_

CFItems.fullStatement: Adapt health messages and communication techniques to a specific target audience.
CFItems.notes: _Example: producing a social media post to encourage a positive health behavior_

CFItems.fullStatement: Leaders in Health Advocacy
Anchor Standard 1: Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health. (Health Promotion)
Research national, state and local data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Youth Risk Behavior Survey for prioritizing prevention activities for the school and community.
Interpret the Youth Risk Behavior Survey data on the six priority adolescent risk behaviors.
Recognize the adolescent risk behaviors of high incidence among Alabama's students.
Anchor Standard 2: Students will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors. (Analyzing Influences)
Analyze how health risk behaviors in the local school and community are influenced by family, peers and other factors.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: availability of alcohol and drugs; trends in adolescent sexual behavior; availability of fast food; access to fitness and recreational facilities._

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 3: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid information, products, and services to enhance health. (Access to Information)
Gather information and interpret data for planning prevention activities.
Identify concerns, beliefs, and areas of misinformation among peers.
Design program goals based on addressing misinformation, beliefs, and concerns among peers.
Utilize a focus group to change their school climate.
Anchor Standard 4: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks. (Interpersonal Communication)
Execute communication and leadership skills to empower other students to be physically, socially, behaviorally, emotionally, and intellectually successful.
Examine the varied roles and responsibilities of student leaders.
Design program goals based on YRBS data and focus group results.
Research various leadership and peer training programs and opportunities.
Apply peer helping training skills in assigned schools settings.
Demonstrate leadership skills by advocating for health-related changes in the school or community.
Anchor Standard 5: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health. (Decision-Making)
Identify decision-making skills used in situations that put adolescents and teens at risk.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: recording a fight and posting it on a social media; seeing a friend smoking marijuana or drinking alcohol; hearing a friend talk about shoplifting; hearing plans about a weekend party that will include drugs and/or alcohol; pressure to have sexual relations_

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify consequences of making poor decisions to join in or ignore risky situations.
Recognize the differences between situations in which one has control vs. a lack of control.
Review the importance of successfully managing decision-making skills when confronted with uncomfortable, risky, or dangerous situations.
Develop and implement a school-wide plan or campaign to encourage good decision-making skills.
Anchor Standard 6: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health. (Goal-Setting)
Conduct a school-wide survey to assess the use of personal health practices.
Compile survey results to develop a school-wide campaign to advocate the use of beneficial personal health practices.
Implement strategies to address weak areas and critical needs based on survey results.
Anchor Standard 7: Students will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks. (Self-Management)
Analyze the role of individual responsibility for enhancing health.
Demonstrate a variety of healthy practices and behaviors that will maintain or improve the health of self and peers.
Identify a variety of behaviors to avoid or reduce health risks to self and others.
Plan a school or community campaign designed to encourage health-enhancing behaviors.
Anchor Standard 8: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health. (Advocacy)
Use school-wide survey data to develop positive messages concerning health topics, including exercise, adequate sleep, and healthy eating.
Lead or participate in community-wide health-related events.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: Relay for Life, 5K run, Longest Day activities (Alzheimer's Association)_

CFItems.fullStatement: Communicate to peer or community groups on health-related topics.
World Health
Anchor Standard 1: Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health. (Health Promotion)
Research the history of disease in the world.
Identify causes of major outbreaks and epidemics in the history of the world.
List major breakthroughs in the prevention and cure of disease.
Assess the effects of current health issues on world populations.
Anchor Standard 2: Students will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors. (Analyzing Influences)
Examine the health challenges facing the world today.
Collect statistical data about health issues within various countries.
Investigate the influence of family, peers, and culture on possible solutions to world health issues.
Examine the links among health, economic development, media, and technology.
Research how disparities in socio-economic status can adversely affect health and access to health care globally.
Analyze the roles and responsibilities of government and non-governmental organizations in achieving global health.
Anchor Standard 3: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid information, products, and services to enhance health. (Access to Information, Products, and Services)
Critique health intervention programs worldwide.
Examine possible solutions to world health issues through available intervention programs.
Anchor Standard 4: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks. (Interpersonal Communication)
Communicate with professionals who support world health to learn about the roles and responsibilities of their jobs.
Research the effectiveness of communicating prevention and management strategies to resolve world health issues.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: HIV/AIDS, mental health, substance abuse, obesity, physical activity, nutrition, hunger_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 5: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health. (Decision-Making)
Evaluate alternatives to current world health programs and practices.
Examine barriers that hinder decision-making skills related to world health issues.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: politics, religious beliefs, culture_

CFItems.fullStatement: Predict the potential short- and long-term impacts of poor decision-making on world health issues.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: rising cost of medical care_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 6: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health. (Goal-Setting)
Research the needs, strengths, and risks of long-term goals for addressing world health issues.
Anchor Standard 7: Students will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks. (Self-Management)
Analyze individual responsibility for enhancing global health.
CFItems.notes: _Example: explaining how individual actions can help or hinder the eradication of communicable diseases_

CFItems.fullStatement: Compare healthy practices and behaviors of people from various world-wide locations.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: immunizations, wellness checkups_

CFItems.fullStatement: Anchor Standard 8: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health. (Advocacy)
Formulate innovative ways to influence and support people in other countries in making positive health choices.
Work cooperatively as an advocate for improving world-wide health.
CFItems.notes: _Examples: participating in international events such as Earth Day and World AIDS Day_

CFItems.fullStatement: Adapt health messages and communication techniques to a specific global audience.
